taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce prostrata is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Flat radiating annual mat with opposite asymmetric leaves and tiny axillary cyathia; fruit and stems are often visibly hairy under magnification.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew explicitly treats Chamaesyce prostrata as a synonym of accepted Euphorbia prostrata Aiton.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae/Euphorbia: milky latex and highly reduced flowers grouped into a cyathium; in sandmat spurges, opposite leaves, stem habit, hairiness, and capsule traits are especially useful.
best_field_traits: capsules often hairy especially along angles
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with E. serpens, E. prostrata is usually coarser and hairier, with more elongated leaves and hairy fruiting structures.
